index.title: Which Unit Sets the Output
index.prompt: A draw of the 13 starting weights of the 4-unit tanh network is given. Evaluate the network at t = 0 and at t = 2, name the unit that contributes most at each, and find the t where one unit sits at the middle of its range. 3 parts.
index.answer: Worked solutions are given part by part on the problem page. Attempt each part on paper before revealing it.

theory.title: Which Unit Sets the Output
overview: A draw of the 13 starting weights is 13 standard normal numbers laid end to end, in the order $w$, then $b$, then $v$, then $c$. This draw is not the seeded one behind the lesson's table, so those table values do not apply here. This time the draw is

prompt.p: Evaluate the network at $t = 0$. Enter the value, and say which unit contributes most to it.

answer.p: At $t = 0$ each unit's argument is its own $b$, so each unit contributes $v_i \tanh(b_i)$:
The four contributions sum to 1.4587, and with $c = -0.9583$ the output is 0.5004.

Unit 4 contributes the most, at 0.8084. Its $v$ is the second largest of the four in size, so the largest $v$ did not decide this value. Unit 2 has the largest $v$ at 1.6348, but its $b$ is only 0.1097, and $\tanh$ of a number that small is 0.1093, so the unit lands at 0.1786, under a quarter of what unit 4 contributes. What reaches the output is $v$ multiplied by how far that unit's argument sits from 0, and the two together decide which unit matters.

prompt.p: Evaluate the same network at $t = 2$. Enter the value, then name the unit that contributes most to it and give its contribution.

answer.p: They sum to −2.2235, so the output is −3.1818.

Unit 2 contributes the most, at −1.6146, and the unit that led at $t = 0$ has fallen to −0.0690. The two have traded places because the arguments have moved in opposite directions. Unit 4's argument went from −0.7848 to 0.0560, through 0 and out the other side, and its contribution is now nearly nothing. Unit 2's argument went from 0.1097 to −2.5391, which is far enough down that $\tanh$ of it is −0.9876, within 1.3% of −1. The weights did not change between the two parts. Which unit matters changed because $t$ changed.

prompt.p: Unit 2 contributes more than any other unit over most of $0 \leq t \leq 2$. At what $t$ does it sit at the middle of its range, and what does it contribute to the output for the rest of the interval?

answer.p: A unit sits at the middle of its range where $\tanh(wt + b) = 0$, which needs $wt + b = 0$. For unit 2 that is

Its contribution is 0 there, positive before it and negative after, and the sign of its $v$ means that it adds to the output early and takes away later. The size of the negative it takes grows quickly: its argument is −0.5525 at $t = 0.5$, −1.2147 at $t = 1$ and −2.5391 at $t = 2$, so the contribution runs −0.8213, −1.3701 and −1.6146. The limit it approaches is $-v = -1.6348$, and by $t = 2$ it is within 1.3% of it.

Across the second half of the interval, $1 \leq t \leq 2$, the contribution moves only from −1.3701 to −1.6146, so there it is close to a constant. The largest weight on the output belongs to a unit that spends most of the interval saturated, and a saturated unit moves the level of the curve rather than its shape. Over most of $0 \leq t \leq 2$ the shape is set by the other three units.
